summary.headline: Refex Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose to INR141 crore (20.1% margin) and PAT to INR94 crore, driven by Ash & Coal Handling and wind turbine deliveries.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 standalone continuing-operations revenue of INR701 crore (+18% YoY) with EBITDA of INR141 crore versus INR62 crore a year earlier, and PAT of INR94 crore (+67%). For FY26, revenue fell to INR2,039 crore from INR2,259 crore as the company exited Power Trading and Refrigerant Gas, while EBITDA rose 68% to INR350 crore (17.2% margin) and PAT reached INR247 crore. Wind turbine deliveries began in February 2026 and contributed about INR233 crore in Q4. The demerger of the mobility business is awaiting NCLT hearing, with management guiding to completion in roughly 60 to 90 days.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR62 crore YoY; margin 20.1% vs 10.4%
+67% YoY vs INR56 crore; PAT margin 13.4%
Initial phase of execution; FY26 wind execution INR238 crore
Excluding discontinued trading revenue; reported segment revenue about INR2,000 crore

segments.name: Ash & Coal Handling
segments.commentary: Q4 segment revenue cited as about INR690 crore; order pipeline about INR1,500 crore including new long-term contracts (e.g., APGENCO 3-year order). Current throughput 68,000 to 70,000 tonnes per day versus earlier guidance of 90,000 to 95,000.

segments.name: Wind (Venwind Refex Power)
segments.commentary: Order book about INR1,860 crore with INR238 crore executed in FY26; management expects to execute the balance (about INR1,500 crore) in FY27. Current EBITDA margin about 8%; 5.3 MW platform; ALMM approval received; capacity target about 2 GW by next year-end.

segments.name: Mobility (EV)
segments.commentary: Crossed INR100 crore revenue in its third year of operation; being demerged via NCLT scheme, with the company stating all its compliances are complete. Shift to asset-light model with clean fuel and enterprise focus.

segments.name: Discontinued: Power Trading and Refrigerant Gas
segments.commentary: Management says it has fully exited Power Trading and liquidated refrigerant gas stock; part of a receivable is still pending and expected to close in the current quarter. Trading revenue reduction of about INR220 crore cited.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Ash & Coal Handling growth in FY27, described as double-digit percentage versus FY26, with no specific numbers given.
Wind: all existing open orders (about INR1,500 crore balance) expected to be executed in FY26/FY27, plus possible new orders; no firm number given for FY27 revenue.
EBITDA margin expected to be sustained at about 15% to 18% (Q4's 20% described as sustainable), per management.
Demerger of mobility business expected to complete in about 60 to 90 days, subject to NCLT hearing timing (first week of June cited).
Finance cost hit of INR2 crore to INR2.2 crore from refinancing; management says there is no capital or working-capital challenge.
capex_capacity: Ash & Coal Handling throughput currently 68,000 to 70,000 tonnes per day; gradual ramp-up toward 90,000 to 95,000 targeted within FY27, with management saying there is no capacity constraint.
Operates across about 40 thermal power plants per management.
Wind capacity targeted at about 2 GW by next year-end, with localization of several products still in progress.
Wind localization is a 1 to 2 year journey expected to improve margins; no margin number given.
demand_pricing: Management says the company is India's largest ash-handling player; second-largest estimated at about 25% of Refex's size; fragmented peers working at 1 to 5 plants each.
Management estimates market share around 3% of a roughly INR75,000 crore TAM and aspires to reach double-digit share over several years.
Diesel cost increase: contracts have escalation clauses that recover about 40% to 60% of costs (pass-through), rest absorbed.
Receivable days guided at 105 to 125 days standalone; wind receivables are short-cycle because they are backed by LCs.
Contract assets (unbilled revenue) were above INR700 crore; management describes it as a running account that is not expected to fall sharply.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the order book stay at INR1,500 crore with Q4 fresh orders of INR120 to 130 crore against Ash & Coal revenue of INR690 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all orders are disclosed; some long-term orders such as APGENCO (3-year) were added at the start of the year and were not reflected in the figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook after the 20% Q4 print?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will be around the same, with a sustainable 15% to 18% range; the 11% to 12% prior guidance referred to net profit, not EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wind EBITDA margin and FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Current wind EBITDA margin about 8%, expected to stay at similar levels; FY27 wind revenue to rise sharply versus FY26's INR238 crore as the INR1,500 crore balance is executed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the promoter pledge increase to 41%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pledges are released on loan closure, with payments made monthly; a large part expected to be removed over about 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a financial or reputational impact from the IT search?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all disclosures were made at each stage and it sees no challenge from the IT matter for the company.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the warrant subscription not taken up and how will funding be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called non-subscription a deliberate decision; it said there is sufficient cash, bank limits and internal accruals, and no immediate fundraise planned.

risks_watch: Demerger timing depends on NCLT hearings; any delay beyond the guided 60 to 90 days would push out value unlocking.
Ash & Coal Handling throughput ramp-up from 68,000 to 70,000 tonnes per day toward 90,000 to 95,000 tonnes per day has not yet been shown; the company's guidance on this shifted between calls.
Wind margins (about 8% EBITDA) are low and depend on localization; new wind orders are not yet firm.
Working-capital intensity: receivable days of 130 to 140 cited by an analyst, and contract assets above INR700 crore.
Promoter share pledge at about 41%, with release contingent on loan repayment.
Finance cost rising (about INR30 crore in FY26 per analyst) and warrant non-subscription by promoter and non-promoter entities.
Diesel cost pass-through covers only 40% to 60% of cost increases.
Ongoing industrial classification change application (filed about 2 months ago) still pending.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and margins, but vague on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to quantify FY27 revenue, wind margins, and EBITDA trajectory. Several answers were inconsistent or defensive (e.g., throughput guidance, the 20% margin sustainability, and the order book discrepancy).
key_quotes: We are confident to have a growth in the current financial year.
EBITDA margin has improved current quarter at 20.1% compared to the previous 10.4% in the corresponding last year.
There is no capacity constraint. Ramp-up only takes time, locations to locations project to project.

adds.what: Wind capacity platform scaling to about 2 GW by next year-end (current 5.3 MW platform)
Ash & coal handling throughput ramp-up from 68,000-70,000 t/day to 90,000-95,000 t/day

growth.why: Management guides double-digit Ash & Coal growth in FY27 and execution of the ~INR1,500 crore wind order balance, backed by a INR1,500 crore ash pipeline and a 1,860 crore wind order book, with throughput ramp to 90-95k t/day in FY27; no numeric FY27 revenue guidance given.
